## Purpose and entry points
SkyRL is a Python monorepo for LLM reinforcement learning: distributed policy training, rollout inference, Gymnasium-style tool-use environments, Tinker-compatible serving, and long-horizon agent pipelines. Primary training entry points are `skyrl/train/entrypoints/main_base.py`, `skyrl/train/main_sft.py`, and `skyrl/train/entrypoints/main_generate.py`; serving is exposed through `skyrl/train/entrypoints/serve.py`.

## Training orchestration
The training layer owns configuration, dataset preparation, rollout collection, optimization, evaluation, callbacks, and tracking. `skyrl/train/trainer.py` is the central RL trainer; `skyrl/train/fully_async_trainer.py` provides decoupled asynchronous rollout/training; `skyrl/train/sft_trainer.py` handles supervised fine-tuning. Config and batch boundaries are defined in `skyrl/train/config/config.py` and `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/training_batch.py`.

## Rollout and environment boundary
Generators convert prompts into model interactions and trajectories, then feed scored samples to trainers. `skyrl/train/generators/base.py` establishes the generator abstraction, while `skyrl/train/generators/skyrl_gym_generator.py` connects training to Gym environments. `skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/core.py` and `skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/registration.py` provide the environment API/registry; bundled math, coding, search, SQL, and RLM environments live under `skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/`.

## Distributed training backend
`skyrl/backends/skyrl_train_backend.py` adapts the unified library to the training implementation. Worker dispatch and backend-neutral worker behavior are centered on `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/workers/worker_dispatch.py` and `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/workers/worker.py`. Distributed strategies support PyTorch FSDP and Megatron through `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/distributed/fsdp_strategy.py` and `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/distributed/megatron/megatron_strategy.py`, including model/optimizer/packing-specific Megatron machinery.

## Inference and weight synchronization
Rollouts are served by an inference-server subsystem: server lifecycle/pooling in `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/inference_servers/server_group.py`, vLLM routing in `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/inference_servers/vllm_router.py`, and remote access in `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/inference_servers/remote_inference_client.py`. Training-to-inference model freshness is a distinct boundary implemented by `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/weight_sync/base.py` with broadcast, CUDA IPC, and transfer strategies. This enables colocated, remote, and fully asynchronous rollout topologies.

## Tinker and native model engine
The `skyrl/tinker/` subsystem implements a Tinker-compatible API/service with engine logic in `skyrl/tinker/engine.py`, request API in `skyrl/tinker/api.py`, and persistent database models/migrations in `skyrl/tinker/db_models.py` and `skyrl/tinker/alembic/`. `skyrl/tx/` is the cross-platform local engine, containing model implementations such as `skyrl/tx/models/qwen3.py`, reusable layers, and loaders; it supports unified training/inference beneath the Tinker-facing interface.

## Agent layer and runtime ecosystem
`skyrl-agent/` is a separately packaged agent framework: agent implementations (`skyrl-agent/skyrl_agent/agents/`), task/tool abstractions (`skyrl-agent/skyrl_agent/tasks/base.py`, `skyrl-agent/skyrl_agent/tools/base.py`), and backends for SkyRL Train, Tinker, OpenAI, and veRL (`skyrl-agent/skyrl_agent/integrations/`). Material runtime dependencies implied by the architecture are Python, PyTorch/CUDA, Ray-based distributed execution, vLLM inference, FSDP/Megatron parallelism, optional JAX backends (`skyrl/backends/jax.py`), and SQL database infrastructure for Tinker. Object-storage I/O is abstracted in `skyrl/backends/skyrl_train/utils/io/s3fs.py`.
